name: Renal Ciliopathy Syndromes

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in cilia-related genes
Presence of bilateral renal cystic disease or renal fibrosis on imaging or histology
Presence of extrarenal features consistent with ciliopathy (e.g., retinal dystrophy, hepatic fibrosis)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic genetic variant in cilia-related gene plus renal cystic disease or fibrosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by extrarenal manifestations and family history

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory infections due to ciliary dysfunction

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal impairment
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing bilateral renal cysts
Liver imaging demonstrating fibrosis or cysts
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes encoding ciliary proteins (e.g., PKD1, PKD2, NPHP genes)
other: Histopathology showing renal interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly cystic kidney disease without multisystem involvement
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Absence of significant cystic kidney enlargement
Frequent extrarenal manifestations such as retinal degeneration

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in a child or young adult
Presence of multisystem involvement including retinal and hepatic disease
Family history of early-onset cystic kidney disease or renal failure
references: Hildebrandt F, Benzing T, Katsanis N. Ciliopathies. N Engl J Med. 2011 Apr 21;364(16):1533-43.
Waters AM, Beales PL. Ciliopathies: an expanding disease spectrum. Pediatr Nephrol. 2011 Jul;26(7):1039-56.
Torres VE, Harris PC. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: the last 3 years. Kidney Int. 2009 Nov;76(5):149-68.
